name: Rahab
charge: Receiving the spies with peace, and believing that the Lord had given Israel the land
summary: A harlot of Jericho hid two Israelite spies under the flax on her roof, confessed that the Lord their God is God in heaven above and in earth beneath, and asked for her father's house. She bound the scarlet line in the window. When the wall fell, hers was the one house left, and she is in the line of Christ.
offense: She was a Canaanite, a harlot, and a resident of a city under the ban, and her faith came by report before it came by sight: we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og (Joshua 2:10). She said what the report had done to the city, and to her: as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man (Joshua 2:11). Faith and fear went together in her. What she feared was not the king of Jericho, who could have had her killed for hiding the men, but the judgment of the God she had heard of, and that fear is what gave her the faith to put her life on the line. Her confession is complete and it is in her own mouth: the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath (Joshua 2:11). She hid the men on the roof under the flax, answered the king's men with truth in part and misdirection in the rest, and sent the pursuers toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere (Joshua 2:4-7). Then she bargained, as one who had something to sell: swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father's house (Joshua 2:12-13). James selects her as the standing example that faith which does not act is dead, and pairs her with Abraham (James 2:25).
judgment: The spies answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business (Joshua 2:14), so the covenant was conditional: if she uttered it, they would be quit of the oath (Joshua 2:20). The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window she had let them down by, and the terms were that everyone in the house behind it would live and anyone who went out of the doors into the street would answer for himself (Joshua 2:18-19). She said, according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window (Joshua 2:21). When the wall fell down flat, her house stood, and Joshua sent the two spies to bring her out with her father, her mother, her brethren, and all that she had (Joshua 6:22-23). Everything else in the city was devoted. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers (Joshua 6:25). Hebrews lists her among those who perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace (Hebrews 11:31), and Matthew places her in the direct line of David and of Christ, Salmon begat Booz of Rachab (Matthew 1:5), so that the woman spared from the ban became an ancestor of the one who ends it.

verses.text: And Joshua the son of Nun sent out of Shittim two men to spy secretly, saying, Go view the land, even Jericho. And they went, and came into an harlot’s house, named Rahab, and lodged there.
And it was told the king of Jericho, saying, Behold, there came men in hither to night of the children of Israel to search out the country.
And the king of Jericho sent unto Rahab, saying, Bring forth the men that are come to thee, which are entered into thine house: for they be come to search out all the country.
And the woman took the two men, and hid them, and said thus, There came men unto me, but I wist not whence they were:
And it came to pass about the time of shutting of the gate, when it was dark, that the men went out: whither the men went I wot not: pursue after them quickly; for ye shall overtake them.
But she had brought them up to the roof of the house, and hid them with the stalks of flax, which she had laid in order upon the roof.
And the men pursued after them the way to Jordan unto the fords: and as soon as they which pursued after them were gone out, they shut the gate.
And before they were laid down, she came up unto them upon the roof;
And she said unto the men, I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you.

For we have heard how the Lord dried up the water of the Red sea for you, when ye came out of Egypt; and what ye did unto the two kings of the Amorites, that were on the other side Jordan, Sihon and Og, whom ye utterly destroyed.

And as soon as we had heard these things, our hearts did melt, neither did there remain any more courage in any man, because of you: for the Lord your God, he is God in heaven above, and in earth beneath.
Now therefore, I pray you, swear unto me by the Lord, since I have shewed you kindness, that ye will also shew kindness unto my father’s house, and give me a true token:
And that ye will save alive my father, and my mother, and my brethren, and my sisters, and all that they have, and deliver our lives from death.
And the men answered her, Our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business. And it shall be, when the Lord hath given us the land, that we will deal kindly and truly with thee.
And the men said unto her, We will be blameless of this thine oath which thou hast made us swear.

Behold, when we come into the land, thou shalt bind this line of scarlet thread in the window which thou didst let us down by: and thou shalt bring thy father, and thy mother, and thy brethren, and all thy father’s household, home unto thee.

And it shall be, that whosoever shall go out of the doors of thy house into the street, his blood shall be upon his head, and we will be guiltless: and whosoever shall be with thee in the house, his blood shall be on our head, if any hand be upon him.
And if thou utter this our business, then we will be quit of thine oath which thou hast made us to swear.
And she said, According unto your words, so be it. And she sent them away, and they departed: and she bound the scarlet line in the window.
But Joshua had said unto the two men that had spied out the country, Go into the harlot’s house, and bring out thence the woman, and all that she hath, as ye sware unto her.

And the young men that were spies went in, and brought out Rahab, and her father, and her mother, and her brethren, and all that she had; and they brought out all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel.
And they burnt the city with fire, and all that was therein: only the silver, and the gold, and the vessels of brass and of iron, they put into the treasury of the house of the Lord.

And Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive, and her father’s household, and all that she had; and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day; because she hid the messengers, which Joshua sent to spy out Jericho.
By faith the harlot Rahab perished not with them that believed not, when she had received the spies with peace.
Likewise also was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers, and had sent them out another way?
And Salmon begat Booz of Rachab; and Booz begat Obed of Ruth; and Obed begat Jesse;

entries.commentary: Joshua sent two men out of Shittim to spy secretly and view the land, even Jericho, and they came into the house of a harlot named Rahab and lodged there. Word made its way to the king of Jericho that men of the children of Israel had come to search out the country, and he sent unto Rahab to bring them forth. She had taken the two men and hid them on the roof under the stalks of flax she had laid in order there. She told the king's men the truth in part and misdirection in the rest: men came unto me, but I wist not whence they were, and they went out about the time of the shutting of the gate; pursue after them quickly. The pursuers chased toward Jordan after men who had gone nowhere, the gate was shut behind them, and the spies had clearance to escape. A heathen woman looked out for Israel, and she did it out of the fear of the Lord, as her own words show.

Before the spies lay down, Rahab came up to the roof and confessed: I know that the Lord hath given you the land, and that your terror is fallen upon us, and that all the inhabitants of the land faint because of you. That is faith and belief; a heathen acknowledged that the God of Israel had ordained them to conquer her land.

Rahab asked the spies to swear unto her by the Lord, since she had shewed them kindness, that they would shew kindness unto her father's house and give her a true token, saving her father, mother, brethren, and sisters alive. The men answered, our life for yours, if ye utter not this our business: since she looked out for Israel, Israel would look out for her, on condition the plan stayed secret. If she uttered the business, the oath was null and void. The token was the line of scarlet thread bound in the window by which she let them down, for her house was upon the town wall. That scarlet line marked her house so no one in it would be slain when Israel came into the land; the terms were that whosoever went out of the doors into the street, his blood would be on his own head, and whosoever stayed within, his blood on Israel's head if any hand touched him. She sent them to the mountain to hide three days until the pursuers returned, said according unto your words, so be it, and bound the scarlet line in the window.

The spies abode in the mountain three days until the pursuers returned, having sought them throughout all the way and found them not. They came again to Joshua and reported: truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land, for even all the inhabitants of the country do faint because of us. The land was theirs for the taking, exactly as the Lord had promised.

Jericho was straitly shut up because of the children of Israel: none went out and none came in. Jericho had a military, and a garrison, a military base, was built there, with the walls shut so nobody could enter or leave. The Lord said unto Joshua, See, I have given into thine hand Jericho, and the king thereof, and the mighty men of valour: the battle was already decided.

The battle plan came from the Lord: compass the city with all the men of war once a day for six days, seven priests bearing seven trumpets of rams' horns before the ark; on the seventh day compass the city seven times, and at the long blast all the people shout with a great shout, and the wall shall fall down flat. The blowing of the trumpets activates the armies of the Lord, the angels, to help in battle. Remember Elisha's servant: when his eyes were opened he saw the host of angels that were there warring and protecting Israel. This is the spirit behind the men of Israel rehearsing the righteous acts with trumpets and shofars today, at the camps and at the new moons; it is spiritual and an act of faith.

Joshua called the priests and gave the order: seven priests bear seven trumpets before the ark, the armed men pass on before the ark, and the rereward, the guards in the rear, came after the ark. Joshua commanded the people, Ye shall not shout, nor make any noise with your voice, neither shall any word proceed out of your mouth, until the day I bid you shout; then shall ye shout. The ark of the Lord compassed the city once, and they came into the camp and lodged there.

They repeated the act six days back to back, rising early, the priests bearing the ark and blowing the trumpets, the armed men before and the rereward after, one compass of the city each day. Every army in the world stole this from the Israelites: the pass and review of the militaries, with their battalions and units, their guidons with the eagle on the tip of the spear, marching round the field sounding off with cadences and trumpets, is patterned after what Israel did here.

On the seventh day they rose about the dawning of the day and compassed the city seven times. There is something about the number seven that the Lord loves; you read about it in Revelation. At the seventh time, when the priests blew with the trumpets, Joshua said unto the people, Shout; for the Lord hath given you the city. The men apply [Joshua 6](/bible/joshua/6) to this day: when a scoffer will not hear the word and thinks to outcry the truth, the brothers say the scripture together with one mind, one body, one spirit. That unity is spiritual, a rehearsal of the righteous acts. Unity and order are what the enemies fear: not gangs and drug dealing, but the so-called Black man, Hispanic man, and Native American man unified in the order of a military, with structure and organization. That is what puts fear in the nations.

The city shall be accursed, even it and all that are therein, to the Lord: only Rahab the harlot shall live, she and all that are with her in the house, because she hid the messengers. She made a covenant with the spies: she would conceal them and assist Israel, knowing the Lord was with Israel, as long as her family was saved when the city fell. Rahab was a Canaanite, a heathen, yet the heathen can be blessed when they do it to benefit Israel; blessed is he that blesseth thee. Rahab is the scripture's own example that a man is justified by works and not by faith only: faith and works go hand in hand, for your actions prove whether you believe. Was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, when she had received the messengers and sent them out another way? As the body without the spirit is dead, so faith without works is dead also. Works by the Bible's own dictionary is keeping his commandments: set your hope in God, forget not his works, but keep his commandments. Words say a lot, but actions always speak louder, and by him actions are weighed. Keep yourselves from the accursed thing, lest ye make yourselves accursed and make the camp of Israel a curse, and trouble it: your individual sins affect the whole nation of Israel, your brothers, your sisters, and the children. That is why we must examine ourselves whether we be in the faith. All the silver and gold and vessels of brass and iron were consecrated unto the Lord, separated and sanctified for his treasury alone: nobody was to gain personally from this war.

The people shouted when the priests blew with the trumpets, and the wall fell down flat. That shout is [Isaiah 58:1](/bible/isaiah/58#v1) in action, cry aloud and spare not: the sound coming out of their mouths with the trumpets broke everything down, like thousands of lions roaring at once. The people went up into the city, every man straight before him, and they took the city and utterly destroyed all that was in it, both man and woman, young and old, ox, sheep, and ass, with the edge of the sword.

Joshua sent the two spies into the harlot's house to bring out Rahab and all that she had, as they sware unto her; they brought out her father, mother, brethren, and all her kindred, and left them without the camp of Israel. They burnt the city with fire and all that was therein; only the silver, gold, and vessels of brass and iron went into the treasury of the house of the Lord. Joshua saved Rahab the harlot alive and her father's household, and she dwelleth in Israel even unto this day, because she hid the messengers. She helped the nation of Israel toward rulership, and that is the only help Israel wants from the other nations: not food stamps, welfare, or reparations, but tell our people who they are, the Israelites the Bible speaks of, the so-called Blacks, Hispanics, and Native Americans, and that we must keep the commandments of the Most High. Whoever does that will receive mercy just as Rahab did.

Joshua adjured them at that time: cursed be the man before the Lord that riseth up and buildeth this city Jericho; he shall lay the foundation thereof in his firstborn, and in his youngest son shall he set up the gates of it. The city was not to be rebuilt. So the Lord was with Joshua, and his fame was noised throughout all the country.
